correctness.rationale: A precise proof of necessity shows that Ferrers red and blue row-neighborhood chains must be strict and in opposite order when the host rows form an inclusion antichain; otherwise the host row neighborhoods would be comparable. An isolated 1 between two 0 entries in any column would violate red or blue nesting. Conversely, partition each column into edges before and after its interval of missing positions; these yield nested Ferrers supports for any host. For G_n, all n cyclic missing-row pairs cannot be embedded in only n-1 adjacent pairs of one row order, implying fp>=3; the two triangular Ferrers classes and a single star partition all permitted edges, implying fp<=3. An induced matching of size 3 would force a triangle in C_n, impossible n>=4, while a size-2 witness exists. The reproducible verifier exhaustively checks 996 antichain-row small binary matrices and n=3..100 constructive instances. These finite runs supplement, do not replace, proofs.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complement columns missing consecutive rows is equivalent to a single row ordering in which two nested colored Ferrers supports can be separated. The antichain hypothesis forces the opposing strict color orders, providing the nontrivial necessity. Overlapping chain covers can retain a shared edge; reassigning such an edge may spoil nestedness, so they cannot be assumed to imply an edge partition.

originality.rationale: Full text of London 2026 studies precisely the edge-disjoint Ferrers invariant but only covers paths, cycles, crown graphs, matching-deleted bicliques, general bounds, and explicitly leaves the two-part decision complexity unresolved. The new antichain-row/complement-column-consecutive-ones equivalence supplies a natural genuine structural subclass, and for n>=5 the Hamiltonian-cycle-deleted complete bipartite families are not special cases of the known matching-deleted/cycle results. Covering literature permitting edge overlaps is not equivalent to a disjoint partition. Comparisons with accessible published research did not reveal a stronger covering statement. Historical priority remains provisional, with the inaccessible original Ma--Spinrad full text and unindexed literature noted.
residual_risks: The 1994 foundational two-chain-cover paper could not be inspected in full; an equivalent unpublished or differently formulated result might exist.
The new criterion is limited to antichain row-neighborhood hosts; it does not solve general two-Ferrers edge partition recognition.
The n=3 matching and n=4 C8 special cases are old; the new natural family starts at n=5.
No independent third-party mathematical or priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The paper introducing the parameter explicitly asks for recognition of two-Ferrers edge partitions. The antichain-neighborhood subclass is broad, structurally natural and recognizable by a one-sided consecutive-ones algorithm. Its characterization is exact, not only a sufficient construction. The cycle-deleted biclique application yields an entire dense connected family with a strict induced-matching gap for n>=5, naturally distinct from prior paths/cycles and matching-deleted constructions. The mathematical motivation precedes and exceeds small finite computations.
